references.text: The Levites were brought near to the Lord to serve the priests and the congregation, but the priestly service was reserved for Aaron and his sons.
The Levites were set apart from the people of Israel to serve in the tabernacle, but not as priests.
The priestly service was given only to Aaron and his sons, while the Levites were to be their helpers.
God chose Aaron and his sons specifically for the priesthood, not the entire tribe of Levi.
God consecrated Aaron and his sons to the priesthood as a divine arrangement.
Korah's claim that the whole congregation was holy reveals the motive behind their pursuit of the priesthood.
God confirmed Aaron's priesthood through the sign of the staff that budded, in response to the rebellion.
No one takes this honor upon himself, but must be called by God, as Aaron was.
Korah's rebellion is mentioned as a warning example against rising up against God's chosen leaders.
